Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-14
Start: 15:00 UTC

Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tom (Skyline Head of ML), Maria (Skyline Platform), Derek (CTO)

Auto-summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modelling. Discussed QPS targets, concurrency patterns, typical prompt/response token distributions, acceptable latency SLOs, security considerations for Private vs Dedicated, and a proposed 48-hour benchmark plan. Next steps: share workload CSV, run dedicated pilot, follow-up after benchmark.

00:00:05 - Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, you all good on audio?
00:00:10 - Tom (Skyline): Yep good here, thanks.
00:00:15 - Maria (Skyline): All set.
00:00:20 - Samir: Cool. Quick agenda 









Quick agenda 

 - quick discovery on what you're trying to validate in the POC, we want to nail down QPS, concurrency, input/output token breakdown, and success criteria. Priya will cover the benchmark plan and config.
00:00:35 - Priya (Redwood): Hi all 





I'll walk through the measurement plan and what we'd need from you.
00:00:42 - Derek (Skyline): Great. For context, Skyline is building invoice auto-reconciliation and fraud detection assistants. We'll likely have two main traffic patterns: 1) short prompts for retrieval/QA (avg 50 input tokens, 20 output tokens) and 2) longer generation for summaries (avg 220 input tokens, 180 output).
00:01:05 - Tom: On traffic: peak is around market open 14:00-16:00 UTC for trading customers, QPS spikes up to ~120 rps for the QA routes, and then background batch jobs every 5-10 minutes that hit summarization at lower QPS but higher concurrency when jobs run 
think 8-10 parallel long-gen requests.
00:01:30 - Maria: Our SREs currently throttle at service edge and we see typical concurrency of 40-60 overall across all routes during peak.
00:01:45 - Priya: Okay that's helpful. Can you confirm percent split across routes?
00:01:50 - Tom: Roughly 75% QA/short and 25% summaries and rerank-ish traffic.
00:01:58 - Samir: So for modelling we'll treat two buckets: short/low-token and long/high-token. For cost and latency tradeoffs we need distribution percentiles too 





 for token lengths and service times.
00:02:15 - Tom: We can get that from logs, we have histograms 



00:02:22 - Priya: For the POC we recommend a 48-hour replay to capture diurnal changes and occasional spikes. We'll run that against a Dedicated 4xA100 config and compare to a 8xA100 stress run. The goal is to validate throughput and tail latency and quantify cost per 1M tokens.
00:02:45 - Derek: Question 

 - do we need to expose our raw data? Security team will ask. We can anonymize and hash identifiers. Also curious about VPC/private offering since regulated customers may require it.
00:02:58 - Samir: Totally 

 - you can anonymize. For POC telemetry we only need token counts, timestamps, and request/response sizes, not PII. On Private vs Dedicated: Dedicated gives isolation within Redwood infra, data logs not shared across customers; Private gives customer-managed VPC. For the benchmark we can run in Dedicated or Private depending on contract.
00:03:18 - Maria: For decision making we need clear success criteria 

 - what metrics will you measure?
00:03:24 - Priya: We'll measure QPS achieved (sustained and peak), p50/p90/p99 latency (generation time), error rate, resource utilization (GPU util, memory), and tokens/sec for each model variant. We'll also capture cost estimate and unit economics 

 - cost per 1k tokens.
00:03:45 - Tom: For us success is twofold: 1) meet latency SLO for QA routes 

 
 - 99th < 500ms total generation time, and 2) keep cost below our threshold (we gave finance target of $X per 1M tokens, will plug exact number).
00:04:05 - Samir: Note on latency 

 
 - generation time depends heavily on model context size and KV cache warm state; our runtime supports prefix caching to dramatically reduce long-session costs for chat-style requests, but for one-off prompts caching helps less.
00:04:25 - Tom: We have a lot of repeated prefixes for QA so caching could help. How do you model that?
00:04:30 - Priya: We'll need an estimate of cache hit rate 
 - if you can provide fraction of repeated prompts or session reuse rate, we can model benefits. For the replay please mark sessions that are repeat-query heavy.
00:04:45 - Maria: We'll instrument logs to flag repeated prompts.
00:04:50 - Derek: On model 
 - do you recommend open model X vs proprietary? And what's quantization tradeoff?
00:04:58 - Priya: We usually start with a production-grade open model we vetted in our catalog; we can try 13B quantized and a 33B or 70B variant for quality checks. Quantization reduces memory/throughput needs but can affect output quality 
 - we'll include a small eval set to confirm.
00:05:18 - Tom: For security/compliance we need SOC2 details and encryption at rest, KMS integration.
00:05:23 - Samir: We'll share SOC2 report and security deck. Redwood supports KMS/HSM and brings audit logs for Dedicated/Private. We'll attach the security docs in the follow-up.
00:05:35 - Priya: Back to traffic modeling 
 - a few clarifying Qs. For short-qa routes what's the average prompt and response tokens? You said 50/20 earlier, any 95th percentile?
00:05:46 - Tom: 95th for QA maybe 180 input and 90 output 
 - occasional long context when they attach previous messages.
00:05:55 - Priya: Good. For long-generation route you said avg 220 in / 180 out 
 - what's p95/p99 there?
00:06:02 - Maria: p95 ~380/300, p99 ~800/600 
 - those are heavy but rare.
00:06:12 - Samir: That's important because tail tokens dramatically increase GPU memory/time. We'll simulate with a mixed distribution to ensure memory spikes are captured.
00:06:22 - Tom: On concurrency, the long jobs run on scheduled batches, so we'll see bursts of 8-12 concurrent long-gen; short-route concurrency drives overall QPS.
00:06:33 - Priya: For the benchmark we will create a scenario: baseline steady QPS at 80rps short + scheduled bursts to 120rps, plus long-gen batches of 10 concurrent every 7 minutes 
 - that should approximate your profile.
00:06:50 - Derek: OK timeline? We'd like results in two weeks if possible.
00:06:55 - Samir: Realistically we need 1 week to set up and configure the Dedicated cluster and instrument the replay, then 48h run, then 2-3 days to analyze 
 - so ~2.5 weeks. If you can provide traffic sample this week, we can accelerate.
00:07:12 - Tom: We'll prioritize.
00:07:18 - Priya: On metrics collection 
 - we'll provide instruction for the replay harness (JMeter/postman or our internal replay script) and the schema for the CSV: timestamp, route, input_tokens, output_tokens, session_id, is_repeat_flag.
00:07:33 - Maria: We'll anonymize session_id.
00:07:36 - Samir: Good. Also note that for cost modeling we need average prompt size because simulated tokens determine billing estimates; we'll produce cost per 1M tokens for the tested configs (4x/8x A100, quantized variants).
00:07:54 - Tom: Can Redwood run the benchmark on our private environment? Our security prefers VPC.
00:08:00 - Samir: We can. Two options: 1) Dedicated in Redwood with strict isolation and audit logs, faster to set up; 2) Private (VPC) which takes longer due to networking and approvals but gives you full control. For initial POC Dedicated is usually faster and adequate for performance validation.
00:08:18 - Derek: We'll try Dedicated first and if OA looks good we'll discuss Private for production.
00:08:23 - Priya: Minor tech note: we'll instrument GPU metrics 
 - util, mem, NVLink usage if possible. Also trace request flow to compute end-to-end latency including network hop. That helps distinguish model generation vs infra overhead.
00:08:38 - Maria: We have per-request tracing at edge, so we can correlate.
00:08:41 - Samir: Great. Any blockers from your side?
00:08:45 - Maria: Legal may request contract tweaks but shouldn't block POC. Security review could ask for more details but we can share SOC2 and KMS info.
00:08:55 - Tom: Finance will want a rough cost estimate up front 
 - even a ballpark is fine.
00:09:00 - Samir: I'll share a cost model and ballpark numbers; final numbers after benchmark.
00:09:07 - Priya: Quick note on model variants 
 - we'll run at least two: quantized 13B and 33B FP16 as a quality/throughput tradeoff. We'll capture generation deltas on a labeled eval set you provide (5-10 canonical prompts).
00:09:25 - Derek: We'll pull 10 representative prompts per route.
00:09:28 - Samir: Perfect.
00:09:30 - Priya: Ok moving to benchmark schedule 
 - proposed steps:
00:09:33 - Priya: 1) Tue: ingest traffic sample and map to replay template
00:09:36 - Priya: 2) Wed-Thu: environment setup + dry run
00:09:40 - Priya: 3) Fri-Sat: 48h production-like replay (we run multiple iterations)
00:09:44 - Priya: 4) Mon: analysis and cost/latency report
00:09:48 - Tom: That timeline aligns if we start next week.
00:09:52 - Maria: One more Q on fallback policies 
 - if Dedicated can't meet peak, can requests be routed to Hosted or a smaller cheaper model?
00:10:00 - Samir: Yes, Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants in other capacity tiers or model sizes. We'll include a suggested routing policy for graceful degradation in the report.
00:10:12 - Tom: Good.
00:10:15 - Priya: A couple of implementation details I want to capture: input/output token sampling, session affinity for caching, max sequence lengths to configure, and retry/backoff logic.
00:10:26 - Maria: For retries we use exponential backoff with jitter.
00:10:29 - Priya: Cool. We'll provide recommended config.
00:10:33 - Samir: Any vendor lock-in concerns?
00:10:36 - Derek: We prefer to keep portability 
 - if we need to move to another on-prem runtime that's a risk.
00:10:40 - Priya: Redwood's runtime exports metrics and can run in Private mode; models and artifacts are kept in standard formats. We'll document what's portable vs tied to our optimizations.
00:10:52 - Tom: OK I think we have enough to start.
00:10:55 - Samir: Recap 
 - deliverables from Redwood: security pack (SOC2, KMS, audit), workload template + replay harness, pilot pricing and SLA, and benchmark plan. Deliverables from Skyline: anonymized 48h traffic sample, short eval prompts.
00:11:10 - Maria: Confirming we'll deliver traffic by 2027-05-21.
00:11:15 - Samir: We'll target a kickoff week of 2027-05-24.
00:11:20 - Tom: Sounds good.
00:11:22 - Derek: Anything else on modeling specifics?
00:11:25 - Priya: One last ask 
 - please include frequency of prompt repetition (session-level reuse) so we can simulate caching gains.
00:11:32 - Tom: We'll add a repeat_flag in the CSV.
